title: Global cohomology evaluation of any realized derived pairing
statement: Let X be a scheme, choose the sheaf derived category with Hom types in the universe of X, and let F,G be module sheaves and p,q natural numbers. There exists a family evaluation indexed by every derived morphism f:F[0] tensor-derived G[0] to (F tensor G)[0], each member an O_X(X)-bilinear map H^p(X,F) times H^q(X,G) to H^(p+q)(X,F tensor G). For every computing pairing D [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data] and every cochain realization t [lem-sc-module-cup-resolution-realization], evaluating its explicitly transported derived map on the classes of cocycles a,b gives the class of any cocycle c whose section is D.pair p q top a b. No normalization of H-zero(f), comparison of two pairings, or equality of input classes is assumed.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, section-cup-product: construction before Lemma 20.31.3 and its global specialization

proof.text: Choose a computing pairing using exists_moduleCupResolutionPairing. For any two computing pairings choose cochain realizations, whose H-zero maps equal the same canonical map. Nonpositive connectivity and injectivity of H-zero on morphisms to degree-zero objects show that their derived maps agree. Apply the equal-derived-maps cocycle class lemma to prove class independence.

Global cycle-to-class maps of computing resolutions are surjective because cycle projections are epi and both comparison maps are iso. The signed Leibniz rule makes the paired section a cycle. Its fixed underlying section determines it uniquely. The sectionwise bilinear pairing and target class linear map form a bilinear map on cycles. Descend it through the two surjective input class maps using class independence, proving the additive and scalar laws by lifting representatives.

Use the descended bilinear map as a constant evaluation family on all supplied derived morphisms. The conclusion imposes no condition away from realized pairings. Lift the classes of any other computing pairing to reference cycles, apply its descent formula and class independence, and obtain the asserted evaluation equation. Neither t nor its normalization is assumed for this last step.

theorem moduleCup_realization_evaluation (F G : X.Modules) (p q : ℕ) :
    ∃ evaluation :
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F) ⊗
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj G) ⟶
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj (F ⊗ G)) →
        (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
          (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).obj G →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
            (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace (p + q)).obj (F ⊗ G),
      ∀ (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
        (t : D.left.integerComplex ⊗ D.right.integerComplex ⟶ D.target.integerComplex)
        (_ht : D.Realizes t)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val →
          evaluation (D.derivedMap t) (D.left.class p a) (D.right.class q b) =
            D.target.class (p + q) c
